reasoning: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in one report (qwen3-235b failed to audit tunarr.conf.d due to an HTTP 400 API error), not by substantive security concerns. The other report (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all 8 files including tunarr.conf.d and found them safe. The package is a standard binary AUR package: PKGBUILD downloads a versioned tarball from official GitHub releases with pinned SHA-256 checksums, .install script only performs version checking, and all systemd/sysusers/tmpfiles/conf.d files are standard configuration. No malicious injection patterns detected.
disagreement_analysis: The inconclusive verdict from qwen3-235b was due to an LLM API failure (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when reviewing tunarr.conf.d, not a security finding. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed the same file and found it to be a benign configuration file. This is a coverage gap, not a substantive disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to review tunarr.conf.d due to API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to ambiguous code' - API failures should trigger retries or fallback, not package-level inconclusive verdicts
When a simple config file fails audit due to transient API error, the tool should recognize this and either retry or weight other successful audits of the same file more heavily
Add retry logic for transient API failures (HTTP 400/500) before marking files as inconclusive
